knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian of an Inverse Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))$, given that

$$
u=8 x\qquad v=y\qquad w=z.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation

$$
T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T$ is $\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}$.

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}$, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$.

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=8 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=1 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\begin{vmatrix}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=8\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=8\left(1\cdot 1-0\right) \\ &=8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}&=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1} \\ &=\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x,y,z real; nonzero constant inverse determinant

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian of an Inverse Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y,z)\to (u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}2\left(y{z}^{2}\right) \\ 4\left(z{x}^{2}\right) \\ 4\left(x{y}^{2}\right)\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$

*Hint: You can assume that $x,y,z>0.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={\left(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}\right)}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have 

$$
u(x,y,z)=2\left(y{z}^{2}\right),\,v(x,y,z)=4\left(z{x}^{2}\right),\,w(x,y,z)=4\left(x{y}^{2}\right).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =2\left({z}^{2}\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =2\left(2yz\right) \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =4\left(2xz\right) & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =4\left({x}^{2}\right) \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =4\left({y}^{2}\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =4\left(2xy\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $2, 4, 4$ multiplies the determinant by $32$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2\left({z}^{2}\right) & 2\left(2yz\right) \\ 4\left(2xz\right) & 0 & 4\left({x}^{2}\right) \\ 4\left({y}^{2}\right) & 4\left(2xy\right) & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =32\left(-{z}^{2}\begin{vmatrix}2xz & {x}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & 0\end{vmatrix}+2yz\begin{vmatrix}2xz & 0 \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy\end{vmatrix}\right)\\  & =32\left(-{z}^{2}(0-{x}^{2}{y}^{2})+2yz(4{x}^{2}yz-0)\right)\\  & =32\left({x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+8{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\right)\\  & =288 x^{2} y^{2} z^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing down $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}$ in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}32\left(9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\right) & =32\left(9{({x}^{3}{y}^{3}{z}^{3})}^{2/3}\right) \\  & =32\left(9{(y{z}^{2}\cdot z{x}^{2}\cdot x{y}^{2})}^{2/3}\right) \\  & =32\left(9(\left(\frac{u}{2}\right)\left(\frac{v}{4}\right)\left(\frac{w}{4}\right))^{2/3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={\left(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}\right)}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{36 \left(u v w\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian of an Inverse Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=2\left(3x+yz\right),\,v=4\left(z\right),\,w=4\left(-y\right).
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={\left(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}\right)}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2\left(3\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =2\left(z\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =2\left(y\right) \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =4\left(1\right) \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =4\left(-1\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $2, 4, 4$ multiplies the determinant by $32$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2\left(3\right) & 2\left(z\right) & 2\left(y\right) \\ 0 & 0 & 4\left(1\right) \\ 0 & 4\left(-1\right) & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =32\left(3\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{vmatrix}\right)\\  & =32\left(3(0+1)\right)\\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={\left(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}\right)}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{96}\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x,y,z real; nonzero constant inverse determinant
